Silly
SIL-ee
adjective
From the Middle English seely, Old English sælig, “happy, blessed, innocent,” which drifted through “harmless” and “helpless” to “simple.” In the KJV it means simple, defenceless, easily led — not the modern “absurd.”

Biblical Definition

Silly in the KJV does not mean goofy or absurd; it means simple, gullible, defenceless — easily led, easily deceived, easily preyed upon. It is the older sense of the word, near to seely, “harmless, helpless,” and it names not a comic figure but a vulnerable one. Paul warns of false teachers who “creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts” (2Ti 3:6) — not stupid women but unstable, undiscerning ones, an easy capture for every smooth deceiver because they have no anchor in the truth. Job uses it of the man undone by his own passions: “wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one” (Job 5:2), the simple soul destroyed by the sins it never guarded against. Hosea makes it a bird: “Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart” (Hos 7:11) — fluttering to Egypt, then to Assyria, trusting every foreign nest and possessing none of the wit to see the fowler. And Solomon gives the very definition: “The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going” (Pro 14:15). There is the silly soul — it believes every word, follows every teacher, is tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine. The remedy is not native cleverness but a mind established in Scripture, that it be no more a child, but able to try the spirits whether they be of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

Simple; harmless; easily led or deceived — not the modern “absurd.”

SILLY, simple; harmless; helpless; easily led or deceived.

From Middle English seely, “happy, innocent, harmless.”

It drifted through “helpless” to “simple”; not the modern “absurd.”

False teachers lead captive silly women (2Ti 3:6).

Ephraim is like a silly dove without heart (Hos 7:11).

Key Scripture

2Ti 3:6 — "For of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts,"

Job 5:2 — "For wrath killeth the foolish man, and envy slayeth the silly one."

Hos 7:11 — "Ephraim also is like a silly dove without heart: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria."

Pro 14:15 — "The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going."

Modern Corruption

An honest drift from “simple and helpless” to “absurd”; the word recovers the danger of the undiscerning soul, easy prey for every deceiver.

expand to see more

To the modern ear “silly” is comic — foolish in a harmless, laughable way — and so “silly women” in 2Ti 3:6 sounds like a slur on their intelligence. It is nothing so light. The AV’s silly is the simple, the gullible, the defenceless: not stupid but undiscerning, an easy capture for the false teacher because the soul has no anchor in the truth. The word names a peril, not a joke — the vulnerability of the unestablished heart that believes every word.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is discernment. Solomon draws the line exactly: the simple believeth every word, but the prudent man looketh well to his going. The silly dove flies to Egypt and then to Assyria, trusting every nest; the silly women are led captive by men who creep into houses. The cure is not native cleverness but a mind established in Scripture, no more a child tossed to and fro with every wind of doctrine, but grown up to try the spirits whether they be of God. God does not leave His own defenceless; He gives them His word, His Spirit, and pastors to establish them, that the simple be made wise and the silly no longer led astray.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

The word means simple, helpless, easily led — not the modern “absurd.”

Usage

"Silly women led captive: not stupid but undiscerning, easy prey for the deceiver."

"Ephraim is a silly dove, fluttering to Egypt and Assyria and never seeing the fowler."

"The simple believeth every word — the silly soul is the one with no anchor in the truth."
